solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suggest work in writing

indicators.note: 'in' puts the short work term inside the piece of writing

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone advises putting a job description down on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea or plan for consideration is to make a suggestion.

clue.text: Athlete runs behind lots of people

indicators.note: 'behind' places the runs abbreviation after the group of people

parts.note: a race is a large group of people sharing descent
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sprinter trails at the back of a big crowd of competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter or other competitor in speed events is a typical athlete.

clue.text: Miniature picture — A Sailing Vessel — by old Spanish artist

parts.note: PIC is a shortened form of picture
SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: A small painting of a ship is attributed to a famous old Spanish master.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism.

clue.text: Type of music some kids adore at the outset

indicators.note: 'at the outset' takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Some children love a certain genre right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaican popular music with offbeat rhythms, a forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Chop end off dining chair

indicators.note: 'end off' removes the final letter of the chair word

parts.note: a carver is a dining chair with arms, used at the head of the table

explanation.surface: Someone saws a leg off a dining-room chair.
explanation.walkthrough: A CARVER is a British term for an armed dining chair, traditionally where the meat carver sat.
explanation.definitionFit: To slice or cut meat into pieces is a way to chop it.

clue.text: Severe reduction in A & E

indicators.note: 'in' puts the reduction word between the two letters

parts.note: taken as the letters A and E
a cut is a reduction, as in a pay cut

explanation.surface: Hospital emergency departments face drastic budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E is the British name for the hospital accident and emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute illness or shortage is serious and intense, hence severe.

clue.text: I reveal foreign girl's name

indicators.note: 'foreign' suggests the letters of the words are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discloses an overseas girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Valerie is a common female first name.

clue.text: Potentially characters in Animal Farm, an unlikely sort of story

definitions.meaning: a rooster and a male bovine could appear among the farmyard creatures in Orwell's novel
a tall tale nobody believes is described with this phrase

explanation.surface: Orwell's farmyard creatures might feature in an incredible tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock-and-bull story is an idiom for an absurd, implausible excuse or tale.

clue.text: Respected lady agreed to stash foreign money

indicators.note: 'to stash' means the agreement word hides the currency inside it

parts.note: 'done!' is said to agree a deal
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An esteemed woman consented to hide overseas cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine form of the senior, most respected member of a group.

clue.text: Weapons found in farmstead

indicators.note: 'found in' says the letters are sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Guns are discovered on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms is the general word for guns and other weaponry.

clue.text: Fruit Ray and Bert cultivated across years

indicators.note: 'across' means the rearranged names lie either side of the years letter
'cultivated' suggests the letters of the two names are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Two gardeners, Ray and Bert, have grown a crop over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' turns RAY and BERT into TA...BERRY, which goes across Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of raspberry and blackberry, bred in Scotland, is a soft fruit.

clue.text: Hire purchase no longer available for carpet

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit
a dish that is off the menu has run out

explanation.surface: A rug bought in instalments has been discontinued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is a verb here: to scold someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for reprimanding them, as is the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Brave reorganisation of Hire Co

indicators.note: 'reorganisation of' says the letters of the firm's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rental company bravely restructures itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing great courage, like a hero, is being brave.

clue.text: Test area in former excavation site

indicators.note: 'in' places the area letter between the two other pieces

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a mine is a site dug for minerals

explanation.surface: Survey a region of an old dig.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect or scrutinise something closely is to test it.

clue.text: For example, one sort of anaesthetic

definitions.meaning: one is an example of a numeral
a more numbing agent, comparative of numb

explanation.surface: A doctor gives an instance of a type of painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced NUM-er: something that numbs more.
explanation.definitionFit: One is a numeral; an anaesthetic makes you more numb, so it is a 'numb-er'.

clue.text: Warlike officer, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' signals the word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal

explanation.surface: A belligerent commander, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means relating to war or fighting, as in martial arts.

clue.text: Good-looking worker, so attached to me

indicators.note: 'attached to' joins the pieces end to end

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An attractive labourer is attached to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome is a synonym for attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Nobleman upset Liberal? That's funny

indicators.note: in a down clue 'upset' turns the nobleman word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a lord is a peer, a nobleman

explanation.surface: A peer is put out by a Liberal, and someone finds it amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry, whimsical way.

clue.text: Little pig and the noise it makes if head's cut?

indicators.note: 'head's cut' removes the first letter of the noise

parts.note: a pig grunts

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a piglet's call losing its start.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest, weakest animal in a litter, especially of piglets.

clue.text: Terribly nice English family member

indicators.note: 'Terribly' suggests the letters of the word are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A very pleasant English relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative.

clue.text: Mild-mannered in attack

parts.note: an offensive is a military attack

explanation.surface: A gentle person somehow involved in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoffensive means causing no harm or offence, hence gentle.

clue.text: Fool turned up in tank top

indicators.note: in a down clue 'turned up' reads the pieces from bottom to top
'top' takes the first letter of the word tank

explanation.surface: An idiot appears wearing a sleeveless vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' gives T from tank; T and IN make TIN, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit, short for nitwit, is British slang for a silly person.

clue.text: Be left with large and ultimately unlovely stomach

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: 'ultimately' takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A person is stuck with a big, unattractive paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the abdomen, the stomach area.

clue.text: Quieter part of distillery

indicators.note: 'part of' says the letters form a section of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A calmer section of a whisky-making plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiller is the comparative of still, meaning calmer or more silent.
